title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 65
paragraphs: When the Persians were put to flight at Plataea by the Lacedaemonians, they fled in disorder to their own camp and to the palisade they had built in Theban territory. It is a marvel to me that, though they fought beside the sacred grove of Demeter, not one of the Persians was found to have entered the enclosure or to have been killed within it — but around the temple, on unconsecrated ground, the greater part of the slain fell. I suppose (if one ought to suppose anything about divine matters) that the goddess herself refused to receive them, because they had set fire to the temple — the so-called “palace” at Eleusis.
